newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil government raises industry investment forecast.
newsitem.headline: Brazil government raises industry investment forecast.

text.p: Investment in Brazilian industry between now and the year 2000 will total 94 billion reais, up from a previous estimate of 63 billion reais, Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles said.

The chemical sector would account for about 16 billion reais of that total, with the food industry investing a further 14 billion reais and the paper and cellulose sector 13 billion reais, Dornelles told reporters.
The forecast was based on prelimary investment plans submitted to the government by the private sector.
The increase from the previous report, which was prepared in January, was due to new investment plans and different data-collecting methods, an aide to Dornelles said.

Total new investment in Brazil by 2000, including the transportation, telecommunications, energy and service sectors, would total 251 billion reais, up from a previous estimate of 220 billion reais, Dornelles said.
